transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a little trouble at work lately. It's probably not a huge deal, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, but... I'm a hairstylist, and lately, my hands just feel like they’re moving through glue. 

Like, even just doing simple things, like sectioning hair or mixing color, it just takes me forever now. I try to speed up, I really do, but... people at the salon have started noticing that I’m just slower than I used to be. It's really embarrassing, honestly, and I just hate feeling like I'm letting my clients down. 

Um, is that the kind of thing you meant? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you noticed any shaking, tremors, or movements that you can’t control in your hands or other parts of your body?

No, no, nothing like that. My hands are completely steady, I promise. I haven't had any shaking or anything weird like that. It's really just the slowness... I'm sorry if I made it sound worse than it is! I just feel a little sluggish, but I have total control over my hands. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?

Um... well, I really don't want to sound ungrateful or anything, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling a little down lately. 

It's probably silly, but most days I wake up and there's just this... this heavy, flat sadness right here in my chest. It kind of makes me feel like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning, if that makes sense? I try really hard to push past it, I promise, and I always try to put on a smile for my clients and friends. I really don't want to be a downer or a burden to anyone. 

Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right information, I just don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual or having trouble getting through the day?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I get a little tired after being on my feet all day at the salon, but I think that's pretty normal, right? I definitely don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or anything. I can still get up and get through my day just fine. 

It's really just that... that slowness with my hands that I mentioned before, but my actual energy levels feel okay. I hope that's a good answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Is that helpful?
Have you found that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once looked forward to?

Um... well, I really don't want it to seem like I'm giving up or not trying. I know I need to be present and positive, especially at work. But... I guess things have felt a little different lately. 

I used to love chatting with my clients, you know? And I’d always try to help out the newer stylists at the salon, just to be supportive. Outside of work, I was always the one organizing hikes with my friends. I really enjoyed all of that. But lately... I don't know, I just kind of keep my head down. I try to avoid people a bit more. It's not that I don't like them! I just... I feel like I don't have that spark in me right now to be the fun, outgoing person they expect. 

I feel terrible about it, honestly. I don't want my friends or my boss to think I don't care. I just don't have the drive for it at the moment. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too negative... I really am trying to get back to my normal self.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... gosh, I hope this doesn't make me sound like I've just been letting things slide. I really have been trying to work through it on my own, you know? But... I guess that heavy, flat feeling... it's been around for a while. 

Probably... um, maybe about a year and two months now? Give or take a little bit. I know that sounds like a long time to just be feeling this way, and I'm really sorry I didn't reach out for help sooner. I just kept thinking I could snap myself out of it if I just tried harder, you know? I really didn't want to bother anyone with it until I absolutely had to. 

Is... is that an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Have you noticed that your movements have become slower or that you feel physically slowed down, like you're moving in slow motion?

Um... well, I know I brought this up a little bit earlier, but... I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being bad at my job. I promise I'm still trying my best every single day. 

But... yeah, I guess I have noticed it. It's mostly my hands. When I'm at work... it feels like my hands are moving through glue. Just simple things, like sectioning someone's hair or mixing up the color in the bowl... it just takes me forever now. I try to speed up, I really do, but it's like my body just won't cooperate. 

A few of the other girls at the salon have even started noticing... they've made a few comments about how I'm just slower than I used to be. I feel so embarrassed about it. I don't want them to think I'm slacking off or anything. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once looked forward to?

Um... I know we touched on this a little bit before, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm just complaining... I really am trying to stay positive. 

But, um... yeah, I guess I have lost interest in a lot of things. I used to be so social. I'd chat with all my clients, and I loved helping out the newer stylists at the salon... I just wanted to be supportive, you know? And on my days off, I was always the one getting my friends together to go hiking. I really did love doing all of that. 

But lately... I just kind of keep my head down. I find myself avoiding people more. It's not that I'm upset with anyone or that I don't care! I just... I don't have that spark in me right now. I just don't have the energy to be the fun, outgoing person everyone is used to. 

I feel so guilty about it, honestly. I don't want my friends or my boss to think I'm blowing them off. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too negative, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you found yourself feeling worse about who you are or feeling like you’re a failure, even when you’re doing your best?

Um... gosh, I really hate to admit this, because I know I should just be stronger, and I don't want you to think I'm just throwing a pity party for myself. I really try to keep a brave face on. 

But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling pretty awful about myself lately. It's just... I keep having these thoughts that I'm just a huge burden on everyone around me. And, honestly, sometimes I feel like I deserve all this... like, feeling this way... because I just haven't been able to keep things together. I couldn't manage my money right, and I'm struggling so much at my job, and even just the basic stuff I'm supposed to do at the salon feels impossible. 

I feel so terrible that I can't just be the reliable employee and friend I'm supposed to be. I really don't want to sound like I'm whining, though. I know I just need to try harder to fix it. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I didn't overshare or make it sound worse than it is.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy anything at all anymore, like even things that used to make you happy?

Um... I don't think so? I mean, I know I just said I'm not doing as much as I used to, and I feel bad about that, but... I wouldn't say I don't enjoy *anything* at all. 

I really try to find little moments to appreciate, you know? Like, a nice cup of coffee in the morning, or when a client is really happy with their haircut... that still makes me smile. I'm definitely still trying to focus on the good things, even if it's a bit harder right now. 

I'm not completely... numb, I guess? I hope that doesn't contradict what I said earlier. I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you. Does that sound okay?
Have you had days where even things you used to really enjoy, like a good cup of coffee or a nice conversation, just don’t feel good anymore?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try really hard not to let it get to that point. I don't want to be someone who just... can't appreciate the little things, you know? 

Even on the harder days, I still try to make myself enjoy that morning coffee, or at least smile when my regular clients tell me about their kids. I really don't want to seem ungrateful for the good things I do have. 

So, I wouldn't say I've had days where *nothing* feels good. I'm really trying to keep a positive attitude about it all. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have other people noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than usual, like there's a delay in how you respond to things?

Um... gosh, I really hate to admit this, because I know I should be moving faster, especially at the salon. I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. I really do try my best to keep up. 

But... yeah, I guess some people have mentioned it. It's just... my hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work lately. Like, even just sectioning hair or mixing color, things I usually do without even thinking, it just takes me forever now. A couple of my coworkers have noticed I’m just... slower than I used to be. 

I feel terrible about it, because I know it affects the schedule, and I really don't want to be an inconvenience to anyone. I'm trying so hard to push through it and speed up. Is... is that what you mean? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm not trying.
Have there been days when nothing seemed enjoyable, not even things you used to really like, such as chatting with friends or a favorite activity?

Um... I know we just talked about this, and I really hope I'm not confusing things or being difficult. I want to be a good patient for you. 

I guess... well, I still try to enjoy the little things, like I said. But maybe I have pulled back a bit from the bigger things. I used to be the one chatting with all the clients, you know? And I'd always try to help the newer stylists when they had questions. On weekends, I'd go hiking with my friends. 

But lately... I don't know, I just don't feel like I have that same spark in me to do all of that. I find myself just keeping my head down at work and... kind of avoiding people. It's not that I don't *want* to be friendly, I just... I don't have the energy for it right now. 

I feel really guilty about it, especially with my friends and coworkers. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad person. I'm just trying to be honest with you about how things have changed. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you had times when even the things you used to really enjoy, like chatting with clients or going on hikes with friends, just didn’t feel good or rewarding anymore?

Um... I know we keep coming back to this, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you a clear enough answer. I really want to be helpful. 

I guess... I mean, I really don't want to say that *nothing* feels good, because that sounds so... ungrateful, you know? Like I'm just giving up, and I really promise I'm not. I still try to force myself to go through the motions. Like, if a friend texts me about a hike, I'll try to think about how nice it used to be. 

But... if I'm being completely honest—and I hope you don't think less of me for this—it just feels like I'm faking it lately. Like I'm smiling at the clients because I know I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel happy about the conversation. It just feels... flat, I guess? 

I feel so bad admitting that. I really am trying to snap out of it. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not just repeating myself too much.
Have you found that things you used to really enjoy, like chatting with clients or going on hikes with friends, no longer feel pleasurable or rewarding to you at all?

Um... I feel terrible because I know you've asked me this a few times now, and I really, really don't want to seem like I'm not listening or not trying to give you what you need. I'm so sorry if I'm being difficult. 

I just... I don't think I can say that *nothing* is rewarding at all. That just sounds so drastic, and I really don't want you to think I'm completely broken or that I've just stopped caring entirely. I haven't, I promise. I still go to work every day, and I still try to be a good friend. 

I guess I'm just... I'm not really sure how to answer it any better than I have. I'm still trying my best to find the good in things. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right without making things sound worse than they are.
Have you found that activities you used to really enjoy, like chatting with clients or going on hikes with friends, no longer feel pleasurable or rewarding to you?

Oh... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm making you go in circles and I'm really trying to be a good patient for you. I know I brought some of this up earlier, and I was trying to focus on the positive, but... I guess if I'm just looking at the facts of what I'm actually doing, you're right. 

I really used to be the one who would chat with all the clients, and I'd always try to help the newer stylists out when they needed it, and I loved going hiking with my friends. But now... I guess I do mostly just keep my head down and kind of avoid people. It's just like I don't have that spark in me anymore to do those things, no matter how hard I try to force it. 

I'm really sorry if admitting that makes me sound awful or lazy. I promise I'm trying my best to get back to normal. Did... did I answer it right this time? I hope that helps you.
